pages.text: When something goes wrong, like a division by zero, the function stops and $(l)raises$() an error. The error goes to the caller, and then up to its caller.
If the error reaches the entry function, the process $(l)crashes$(). Mistakes in the program itself, like a wrong indentation, crash it at once.
To catch an error, add a variable of type ERROR to the CALL line. The caller then goes on, and you can check the error's $(1)code$(), $(1)message$(), $(1)context$() and $(1)line$().
$(1)VARIABLE problem ERROR$(br)CALL fail problem$(br)ASSIGN code problem.code ;$()
